div.head: Whiston’s chapter headings (compiled index)
div.note: These headings are transcribed from the 1856 Auburn and Rochester printing of William Whiston’s translation. Their arrangement as an index is editorial; this is not a reproduction of an original printed table of contents.
div.head: BOOK XVII.
div.p: CONTAINING THE INTERVAL OF FOURTEEN YEARS.
FROM ALEXANDER AND ARISTOBULUS'S DEATH TO THE BANISHMENT OF ARCHELAUS.

list.label: I
list.item: HOW ANTIPATER WAS HATED BY ALL THE NATION [OF THE JEWS] FOR THE SLAUGHTER OF HIS BRETHREN; AND HOW, FOR THAT REASON, HE GOT INTO PECULIAR FAVOUR WITH HIS FRIENDS AT ROME, BY GIVING THEM MANY PRESENTS; AS HE DID ALSO WITH SATURNINUS, THE PRESIDENT OF SYRIA, AND THE GOVERNORS WHO WERE UNDER HIM; AND CONCERNING HEROD'S WIVES AND CHILDREN.
list.label: II
list.item: CONCERNING ZAMARIS, THE BABYLONIAN JEW; CONCERNING THE PLOTS LAID BY ANTIPATER AGAINST HIS FATHER; AND SOMEWHAT ABOUT THE PHARISEES.
list.label: III
list.item: CONCERNING THE ENMITY BETWEEN HEROD AND PHERORAS; HOW HEROD SENT ANTIPATER TO CÆSAR; AND OF THE DEATH OF PHERORAS.
list.label: IV
list.item: PHERORAS'S WIFE IS ACCUSED BY HIS FREED-MEN AS GUILTY OF POISONING HIM; AND HOW HEROD, UPON EXAMINING OF THE MATTER BY TORTURE, FOUND THE POISON; BUT SO THAT IT HAD BEEN PREPARED FOR HIMSELF BY HIS SON ANTIPATER; AND, UPON AN INQUIRY BY TORTURE, HE DISCOVERED THE DANGEROUS DESIGNS OF ANTIPATER.
list.label: V
list.item: ANTIPATER'S NAVIGATION FROM ROME TO HIS FATHER; AND HOW HE WAS ACCUSED BY NICOLAUS OF DAMASCUS, AND CONDEMNED TO DIE BY HIS FATHER, AND BY QUINTILIUS VARUS, WHO WAS THEN PRESIDENT OF SYRIA; AND HOW HE WAS THEN BOUND TILL CÆSAR SHOULD BE INFORMED OF HIS CAUSE.
list.label: VI
list.item: CONCERNING THE DISEASE THAT HEROD FELL INTO, AND THE SEDITION WHICH THE JEWS RAISED THEREUPON; WITH THE PUNISHMENT OF THE SEDITIOUS.
list.label: VII
list.item: HEROD HAS THOUGHTS OF KILLING HIMSELF WITH HIS OWN HAND; AND A LITTLE AFTERWARDS HE ORDERS ANTIPATER TO BE SLAIN.
list.label: VIII
list.item: CONCERNING HEROD'S DEATH, AND TESTAMENT, AND BURIAL.
list.label: IX
list.item: HOW THE PEOPLE RAISED A SEDITION AGAINST ARCHELAUS, AND HOW HE SAILED TO ROME.
list.label: X
list.item: A SEDITION OF THE JEWS AGAINST SABINUS; AND HOW VARUS BROUGHT THE AUTHORS OF IT TO PUNISHMENT.
list.label: XI
list.item: AN EMBASSAGE OF THE JEWS TO CÆSAR; AND HOW CÆSAR CONFIRMED HEROD'S TESTAMENT.
list.label: XII
XIII
list.item: HOW ARCHELAUS, UPON A SECOND ACCUSATION, WAS BANISHED TO VIENNA.
